history.feedback:
You have good material and a natural conversational style, but the answer loses clarity because you keep restarting sentences and adding details without a clear hierarchy.

Area	Score
Clarity	6/10
Structure	5/10
Confidence	6/10
Vocabulary	6/10
Conciseness	5/10
Grammar	6/10
Overall	6/10
1. Three specific strengths
You gave concrete examples. The speaking app and miniature flower shop make your answer memorable rather than generic.
You covered multiple dimensions of an enjoyable weekend: rest, exercise, friends, creativity, and family.
Your ideas sound personal and authentic. You aren't relying on memorized or overly sophisticated language, which is good for speaking.
2. Three specific improvements
Stop restarting sentences.
You frequently use “So…,” “Um…,” “Apart from this…,” “Generally…” to buy thinking time. Some fillers are normal, but here they interrupt your ideas.
Instead of: “So generally my weekend is… The days that I get off…”
Say: “My ideal weekend is mainly about resetting mentally and physically.”
Group your ideas instead of listing them randomly.
You move from chores → running → friends → projects → family → games. The listener has to construct the structure themselves.
Use simpler, more accurate phrasing.
A few phrases sound translated or improvised:
“the days that I get off from my company” → “my days off from work”
“the most days that I reserved for reset” → “I reserve these days to reset”
“a app” → “an app”
“small, small projects” → “small creative projects”
“my weekend generally goes” → “my weekend usually goes”
3. A stronger structure

Use a simple purpose → three parts → conclusion structure:

Opening:

“My ideal weekend is a balance between relaxing, being social, and doing something creative.”

Part 1 — Reset:
Sleep in, clean your space, run/exercise.

Part 2 — People:
Meet friends, go to cafés/restaurants, spend time with family.

Part 3 — Creativity:
Work on a small personal project. Give one example.

Conclusion:

“So by Sunday evening, I feel rested, connected, and ready for Monday.”

That would make the same content feel much more organized without requiring more vocabulary.

4. Short improved example
Improved Speaking Example

My ideal weekend is a balance between resting, spending time with people, and doing something creative.

First, I like to use the weekend to reset mentally and physically. I usually sleep in a little, clean my room, organize my desk, and go for a run.

I also like to spend time with friends and family. I might meet my friends at a café or restaurant, and at home, my family and I usually watch movies or play board games like Catan or Monopoly Deal.

The other thing I really enjoy is working on small creative projects. For example, this weekend I built a small app to help people practice speaking. Another weekend, I made a miniature flower shop that my friends had gifted me.

So, for me, a great weekend is one where I can rest, connect with people, and create something. By Monday, I feel refreshed and ready to get back to work.

5. Your focus for the next speaking session

Practice finishing one idea before starting the next.

For your next answer, use this rule: one sentence = one complete idea. And whenever you feel the urge to say “So… um… apart from this…”, pause for one second instead.

Your biggest opportunity isn't vocabulary right now. It's organizing your thoughts while speaking. Once that improves, your existing vocabulary will sound much stronger.
